On the ACME cross-polination point.
I have personally read section 9, and the core mechanism of:

If the certificate chain is not yet available, the "acme-optional-alternate" URL SHOULD serve an HTTP 202 (Accepted) response, with a Retry-After header (Section 10.2.3 of [RFC9110]) estimating when it will become available.

makes sense to me, but I don't own an ACME Client or Server impl, so I just want to make sure that the people who do have given their :+1: that this is a reasonable thing to do.

Bob / David, can you remind me why you don't need a LandmarkDistributionPoint X.509 extn in WebPKI?

chat.author: David Benjamin
chat.text:
OCSP stapling is isomorphic to short-lived certs for the server operator because, one way or another, they have to ping the CA that frequently. And they're isomorphic for the relying party in that they give you a hard upper bound on revocation time, rather than best-effort-RP-push.
They're different for the CA and monitors in that the infrastructure is different. So the sliver of use cases is when that infrastructure becomes the limiting factor for revocation, rather than server operator pings.
